title: Artificial Intelligence Investments by Sovereign Wealth Funds and Their Impact on Economic Diversification: A Comparative Study of the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia and Selected Global Sovereign Wealth Funds
content: Sovereign wealth funds (SWFs) have evolved from passive stabilization instruments into active architects of national economic transformation, and artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as the newest arena in which that transformation is contested. This paper examines how SWFs deploy AI-related capital to advance domestic economic diversification, using a comparative case-study design that places Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) alongside five global peer complexes: Norway's Government Pension Fund Global (GPFG), Singapore's GIC and Temasek Holdings, the United Arab Emirates' Mubadala Investment Company, the Qatar Investment Authority (QIA), and the China Investment Corporation (CIC). Although scholarship on SWF governance and financial performance is extensive, little of it systematically links AI-specific investment mandates to measurable domestic diversification outcomes across funds with structurally different mandates. Employing a mixed-methods design that combines thematic analysis of strategic and governance documents with a simulated comparative analysis of financial and non-oil GDP indicators, the paper develops a four-cluster conceptual framework connecting governance architecture, AI investment behavior, absorptive capacity, and diversification outcomes. Results indicate that PIF exemplifies a pioneering dual-mandate development-finance model—most visibly through its 2025 launch of HUMAIN, a sovereign AI champion spanning the full AI value chain—that differs structurally from all five peers and positions Saudi Arabia among the global first movers in sovereign AI capacity-building. The discussion argues that the diversification value of sovereign AI investment depends not on capital volume but on the alignment among governance design, mandate flexibility, and domestic absorptive capacity—an alignment that Vision 2030's integrated reform program is distinctively structured to achieve. Implications are drawn for policymakers, fund managers, and future comparative research.
